title: Categorical $G = \mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times \mathrm{U}(1)_Y$ action on the Frobenius–Hopf substrate
html:
Conjecture. Categorical G = \mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times \mathrm{U}(1)_Y action on the Frobenius–Hopf substrate

We propose that the Frobenius–Hopf substrate A in \mathbf{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)) admits a unique G-equivariant structure under G = \mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times \mathrm{U}(1)_Y. This structure is governed by four constraints linking the categorical data to the electroweak sector. From these constraints, the symmetric-channel Frobenius trace \mathcal{N}_{\rm sym}(q) = \mathrm{tr}_F(e_{\rm sym}^{\rm EW} \cdot e_H) is computable in closed form.

The four constraints

Constraint (G-1) — G-isotypic decomposition. The substrate A decomposes as a direct sum of G-isotypic components:

  A \;=\; A^{(\gamma)} \;\oplus\; A^{(W^+)} \;\oplus\; A^{(W^-)}
  \;\oplus\; A^{(Z)} \;\oplus\; A^{(H)} \;\oplus\; A^{(\rm matter)}

where each A^{(X)} carries a unique irreducible representation of G. See Table 1.

Constraint (G-2) — Per-host q-dimension assignment. The categorical q-dimension of each component is determined by its torus-link host:

  \dim_q\bigl(A^{(W^\pm)}\bigr) \;=\; [4]_q,
  \qquad
  \dim_q\bigl(A^{(Z)}\bigr) \;=\; [6]_q,
  \qquad
  \dim_q\bigl(A^{(H)}\bigr) \;=\; [2]_q.

The W-host scale [4]_q reflects the T(2,4) crossing count, and the Z-host scale [6]_q reflects T(2,6). The Higgs scale [2]_q is the q-dimension of the fundamental representation, restricted to the neutral component.

Constraint (G-3) — Higgs vacuum vortex morphism. The Higgs vacuum value \langle\Phi\rangle \in A is the unique non-zero vortex morphism \varrho_\Phi \colon \mathbf{1} \to A^{(H)} satisfying

  Q \cdot \varrho_\Phi = 0, \qquad
  \mathrm{tr}_F(\varrho_\Phi^* \cdot \varrho_\Phi) = v^2 / m_e^2,

where Q = T_3 + Y is the unbroken charge generator and v \approx 246\,\mathrm{GeV} is the weak vacuum expectation value. The first condition forces neutrality under the unbroken \mathrm{U}(1)_{\text{em}}. The second fixes the categorical norm to the empirical Higgs VEV.

Constraint (G-4) — Higgs idempotent. The categorical Higgs idempotent e_H is defined from \varrho_\Phi by:

  e_H \;=\; \frac{\varrho_\Phi \cdot \varrho_\Phi^*}{\mathrm{tr}_F(\varrho_\Phi^* \cdot \varrho_\Phi)}.

This rank-1 projector isolates the unbroken 1-dimensional subspace of A^{(H)}. By Constraint (G-2), its trace dimension is [2]_q.

Derivation of \mathcal{N}_{\rm sym}(q)

We compose the traces over the components:

  \mathrm{tr}_F\bigl(e_{\rm sym}^{\rm EW} \cdot e_H\bigr)
  \;=\;
  \dim_q(e_{\rm sym}^{\rm EW}\bigl[A^{(W^+)} \oplus A^{(W^-)} \oplus A^{(Z)}\bigr]) \;\cdot\;
  \dim_q\bigl(e_H \cdot A^{(H)}\bigr).

Applying the assignments from the first two constraints yields:

  • \dim_q(e_{\rm sym}^{\rm EW}[A^{(W^\pm)}]) = [4]_q
  • \dim_q(e_{\rm sym}^{\rm EW}[A^{(Z)}]) = [6]_q
  • \dim_q(e_H \cdot A^{(H)}) = [2]_q

Thus,

  \mathcal{N}_{\rm sym}(q)
  \;=\;
  [4]_q \cdot [4]_q \cdot [6]_q \cdot [2]_q
  \;=\;
  [2]_q \cdot [4]_q^2 \cdot [6]_q.

This derivation grounds Anchor II explicitly in categorical structures. See Table 2.

Verification

At the value q_0 = 1.10998\ldots, the predicted trace evaluates to:

  [2]_q \cdot [4]_q^2 \cdot [6]_q \;=\; 2.0109 \cdot 16.892 \cdot 6.388
  \;\approx\; 216.96.

Compared to the CODATA target \mathcal{N}_{\rm sym}(q_0) = 213.11, this leaves a residual deviation of -1.81\%.

The small discrepancy suggests an incomplete specification of the constraints. Possible physical origins include a categorical correction to the vacuum volume normalization, a Plancherel weight for the electroweak block, or a Higgs-mixing correction of order \mathcal{O}(\hbar_q^2) on the Z-host. Precise discrimination requires refining the substrate's categorical structure.

What rests on this residual

A significant number of the results below are conditional on resolving this residual. See Table 3.
